recipe.name: Smoke-Roasted Chicken Drumsticks
directions: Buy the best chicken you can find, preferably organic. One brand we like after using it on the set of Project Smoke is Smart Chicken.

Remove any loose pieces of cartilage at the joints with poultry shears or a sharp knife. Also be on the lookout for pinfeathers the pluckers may have missed. Remove them with paper towels or kitchen tweezers.
Submerge the drumsticks in brine (1/2 cup of kosher salt per 2 quarts of water) for 24 hours before smoking or grilling. You can cut the time down to as little as 4 hours.
If the skin has receded from the thickest end of the drumstick, gently coax it back before arranging the legs on the grill grate.
Dry the legs with paper towels after removing them from the brine. Place a cooling rack over a rimmed baking sheet, and if desired, air-dry the legs (uncovered) in the refrigerator for several hours.
Set up your grill or smoker for indirect grilling and preheat to 375 degrees.
Arrange the legs in a single layer on the grill grate, rounded side up (the flatter side is the side closest to the body).

Cook the chicken to an internal temperature of 175 to 185 degrees using an instant-read meat thermometer inserted in the thickest part of the leg, being careful not to touch bone with the tip of the probe.
Make the Maple-Sriracha Glaze while the chicken cooks. Keep warm. Apply during the last 10 minutes of cooking and again before serving.
